Getting Unstuck, One Tiny Step at a Time

For the task you keep putting off and the guilt that grows around it. Each day asks for one tiny, specific step on something you have been avoiding, so momentum comes back without needing a burst of willpower.

Motivation · Motivation · Perfectionism · one to-do a day · you choose how many days

Start this challenge free

The first seven days

  • Day 1Write down the one thing you have been avoiding most. Just the name of it.
  • Day 2Spend two minutes on that thing, then stop. Two minutes counts.
  • Day 3Break the thing you are avoiding into five steps, each small enough to do in ten minutes.
  • Day 4Do the first of those steps today.
  • Day 5Set a timer for ten minutes and work on the avoided task until it rings.
  • Day 6Tell someone what you are going to do today, and then do it.
  • Day 7Do the easiest version of the task: a rough draft, a quick call, an ugly first attempt.

Further into the year

The to-dos keep changing as the year goes on. A few from later in this theme:

  • Day 30Look at everything you have done during this challenge and decide the next single step. Write it on a card for tomorrow.
  • Day 60Pick one form and answer only the questions you can answer without looking anything up.
  • Day 120Do the next step with your phone in a different room.
  • Day 240Wipe down, dust, or clear the area where the repair needs to happen, so the next step has room.
  • Day 365Say thank you to yourself for every step this year, then decide the next single one and write it somewhere you will find it tomorrow.

How a challenge works

A Theraglee challenge is a theme with one small to-do for every day of a year. You choose how long yours runs, anywhere from a week to the full year, and each day you get the next to-do: something that takes a few minutes and fits inside an ordinary day. Tick it off when it is done. Nothing is scored and nothing is lost if you miss a day; the next to-do is simply waiting when you come back.

Challenges come with a free Theraglee account, which never asks for a card. Your progress stays private to you.
